newsitem.title: LEBANON: More Sierra Leone evacuees to return to Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: More Sierra Leone evacuees to return to Lebanon.

text.p: A Middle East Airlines airliner left Beirut for Guinea on Monday to bring back some 500 Lebanese refugees who escaped the coup in Sierra Leone, an airport official said.
"The jumbo will fly to Conakry to bring back about 500 Lebanese who have taken refuge at the Lebanese embassy or in hotels there. It is due to return by Wednesday night," he said.
It will be the third plane of Lebanon's national airline to arrive carrying Lebanese evacuees in a week.
Some 180 Lebanese evacuees arrived earlier on Monday, most of them women and children.
"Those are not soldiers, those are barbarians," Kalthoum Murad, 42, said of the soldiers of coup leader Major Johnny Paul Koromah.
Last Thursday, 242 Lebanese arrived on board an MEA plane with the bodies of two compatriots killed during the coup.
Businessman Fuad Ra'ad, said on Monday he had lost everything by leaving Sierra Leone.
"I am a businessman, I have lived in Sierra Leone for 32 years. All my property was stolen but I succeeded in bringing my wife and four children alive," he said.
According to the Lebanese Foreign Ministry there are 2,000 Lebanese living in Sierra Leone but Minister of Immigrants Talal Arslan said on Friday the total was 9,000, mostly businessmen.
Many took shelter at the Lebanese embassy in Freetown, but a woman who arrived in Beirut last week said the status of about 500 Lebanese living outside the capital was unknown.
